BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT (BRD)

Online Banking Application

Document Version: 1.0

Document Type: Business Requirements Document

Purpose: QA practice document — create your own test cases from the requirements below.

1. Business Objective

The Online Banking Application shall allow registered bank customers to securely access their accounts through a web browser and perform common banking activities such as viewing balances, managing beneficiaries, transferring funds, paying bills, and managing credentials.

2. Scope

In Scope:

Customer registration and authentication

Customer dashboard and account balance

Transaction history and filtering

Beneficiary management

Fund transfer and OTP verification

Utility bill payment

Password management and password recovery

Logout and session timeout

Administrator customer management

Notifications and audit logging

Out of Scope:

Opening a new physical bank account

Loan processing

Credit-card application

Cash deposit or withdrawal through physical branches

3. User Roles

Customer — accesses personal banking services and transactions.

Administrator — manages customer account status and authorized customer information.

4. Functional Business Requirements

BR-001: Customer Registration

The system shall allow a new customer to register for online banking using Customer ID, Full Name, Mobile Number, Email Address, Account Number, Date of Birth, Username, Password, and Confirm Password.

Business Rules:

All mandatory fields must be completed.

Customer ID must belong to an existing bank customer.

Account number must be valid.

Mobile number must contain 10 digits.

Email address must be in a valid format.

Username must be unique.

Password and Confirm Password must match.

Password must contain at least 8 characters.

A customer who already has online banking access must not register again.

BR-002: Customer Login

The system shall allow registered customers to log in using a username and password.

Business Rules:

Username and password are mandatory.

Valid credentials shall open the customer dashboard.

Invalid credentials shall display an appropriate error message.

The account shall be temporarily locked after 5 consecutive unsuccessful login attempts.

A locked customer shall not be allowed to log in until unlocked.

Password characters shall not be displayed in plain text.

BR-003: Customer Dashboard

After successful login, the customer shall be redirected to a dashboard showing customer name, masked account number, account type, available balance, current balance, recent transactions, beneficiary information, fund transfer, and bill payment options.

BR-004: Account Balance

The system shall allow customers to view available balance, current balance, account type, and last updated date and time.

Business Rules:

The displayed balance must match the latest balance maintained by the banking system.

BR-005: Transaction History

The customer shall be able to view previous transactions containing Transaction ID, transaction date, transaction type, description, debit amount, credit amount, and closing balance.

Business Rules:

Customers shall be able to filter transactions by date range and transaction type.

Customers shall be able to filter by Debit or Credit.

Transactions shall be displayed in descending order of transaction date.

BR-006: Add Beneficiary

The customer shall be able to add a beneficiary using Beneficiary Name, Account Number, Confirm Account Number, Bank Name, IFSC Code, and Nickname.

Business Rules:

All mandatory fields must be completed.

Account number and Confirm Account Number must match.

IFSC code must follow the valid bank IFSC format.

A beneficiary account cannot be added more than once.

A confirmation message shall be displayed after successful addition.

A newly added beneficiary may require verification before transfer is enabled.

BR-007: Fund Transfer

The customer shall be able to transfer money to an active beneficiary by selecting a beneficiary, source account, transfer amount, transfer type, and remarks.

Business Rules:

Transfer amount must be greater than zero.

Transfer amount must not exceed available balance.

Beneficiary must be active.

Customer must confirm the transaction before submission.

OTP is required for transaction confirmation.

Successful transactions shall generate a unique Transaction ID.

Account balance shall be updated after a successful transfer.

A failed transaction shall not deduct money from the customer's account.

BR-008: Transfer Limits

The system shall enforce transaction limits.

Business Rules:

Maximum single transaction amount is ₹50,000.

Maximum daily transfer amount is ₹1,00,000.

Transactions exceeding a permitted limit shall not be processed.

An appropriate message shall be displayed when a limit is exceeded.

BR-009: OTP Verification

The system shall generate an OTP for sensitive transactions.

Business Rules:

OTP shall be sent to the registered mobile number.

OTP shall contain 6 digits.

OTP shall remain valid for 5 minutes.

Expired OTPs shall not be accepted.

Incorrect OTP shall display an error message.

After multiple unsuccessful OTP attempts, the transaction shall be blocked.

BR-010: Bill Payment

The customer shall be able to pay utility bills for Electricity, Water, Mobile, Internet, and Gas.

Business Rules:

Customer must provide biller, consumer/customer number, payment amount, and payment account.

Payment amount must be greater than zero.

Account must have sufficient balance.

Valid customer/consumer details must be provided.

OTP verification shall be required.

Successful bill payment shall generate a transaction reference number.

BR-011: Change Password

The customer shall be able to change the login password using Current Password, New Password, and Confirm New Password.

Business Rules:

Current password must be correct.

New password and Confirm New Password must match.

New password must contain at least 8 characters.

New password must contain uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.

New password must not be the same as the current password.

Customer shall be notified after successful password change.

BR-012: Forgot Password

The system shall provide a Forgot Password option using registered username and mobile number.

Business Rules:

The system shall verify the customer details.

OTP shall be sent to the registered mobile number.

Customer shall be allowed to create a new password after successful OTP verification.

New password must satisfy the password policy.

Invalid customer information shall not allow password reset.

BR-013: Logout

The customer shall be able to log out of the application.

Business Rules:

Logout shall terminate the active session.

Customer shall be redirected to the login page.

Protected pages shall not be accessible through browser Back after logout.

A new login shall be required to access the dashboard.

BR-014: Session Timeout

The system shall automatically terminate inactive customer sessions.

Business Rules:

Session shall expire after 15 minutes of inactivity.

Customer shall be redirected to the login page after expiry.

Customer must log in again to access protected pages.

BR-015: Account Locking

The system shall protect customer accounts from unauthorized access.

Business Rules:

Account shall be locked after 5 consecutive incorrect login attempts.

Customer shall receive an account-lock notification.

Locked account shall not allow login.

Administrator shall be able to unlock the account.

BR-016: Administrator Customer Management

The administrator shall be able to search customers and view, activate, deactivate, lock, or unlock customer accounts.

Business Rules:

Only authorized administrators may perform administrative actions.

Administrators shall not modify sensitive customer information without authorization.

BR-017: Account Deactivation

An administrator shall be able to deactivate a customer account.

Business Rules:

Deactivated customers shall not be able to log in.

Existing customer sessions should be terminated.

Customer data shall remain available for authorized administrative purposes.

Administrator must provide a reason for deactivation.

BR-018: Notifications

The system shall generate notifications for important customer activities.

Business Rules:

Notifications shall be generated for successful login.

Notifications shall be generated for failed login attempts.

Notifications shall be generated for account locking.

Notifications shall be generated for beneficiary addition.

Notifications shall be generated for successful and failed fund transfers.

Notifications shall be generated for successful bill payments.

Notifications shall be generated for password changes.

Notifications may be sent through registered email and mobile number.

5. Non-Functional Requirements

NFR-001: Performance

The application shall provide acceptable response times under normal system load.

Business Rules:

Login response should be provided within 3 seconds.

Account balance should load within 3 seconds.

Transaction history should load within 5 seconds.

NFR-002: Security

The application shall protect customer credentials and sensitive information.

Business Rules:

Passwords must be securely stored.

Sensitive information must be masked where appropriate.

HTTPS must be used.

OTP must be required for sensitive transactions.

Unauthorized users must not access protected pages.

NFR-003: Availability

The application should be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, except during scheduled maintenance.

NFR-004: Browser Compatibility

The application should support commonly used browsers.

Business Rules:

Google Chrome

Microsoft Edge

Mozilla Firefox

Safari

NFR-005: Usability

The application should provide a clear and consistent user experience.

Business Rules:

Clear error messages should be displayed.

Mandatory fields should be clearly identified.

Navigation should be simple and consistent.

The application should support desktop and mobile screens.

6. Error Handling Requirements

Display an appropriate message when mandatory fields are empty.

Display an appropriate message when invalid data is entered.

Display an appropriate message for incorrect login credentials.

Reject incorrect or expired OTPs.

Reject fund transfers when balance is insufficient.

Reject transfers when transaction limits are exceeded.

Reject invalid beneficiary details.

Redirect the customer when the session expires.

Do not expose sensitive system information in error messages.

7. Audit Requirements

The system shall maintain an audit trail for important activities.

Login attempts

Logout

Beneficiary creation

Fund transfers

Bill payments

Password changes

Account locking and unlocking

Account activation and deactivation

Each audit record should contain the relevant date, time, user, and activity information.

8. Assumptions

Customers already have a valid bank account.

Customers have a registered mobile number.

Customers have internet access.

OTP services are available.

Banking services are available during transactions.

Only authorized administrators can manage customer accounts.

Use this document as the requirement source. Do not use any pre-written test cases. Derive your own positive, negative, boundary-value, validation, security, usability, and integration test scenarios from each requirement.

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT

Ganesh Chaturthi Campaign — “Make a Wish” (#BappaKeLiyeWishList)

Layer 1 — Problem & Intent

1. Problem Statement

Capital Now wants a festive, in-app moment tied to Ganesh Chaturthi that gives eligible users a lightweight, emotionally resonant way to engage with the app (“make a wish”), while running a low-effort, date-driven content campaign that transitions automatically through submission, reveal, and winner-announcement phases without manual operational intervention.

The flow is fully specified by calendar date (14–25 Sept, 26–29 Sept, 30 Sept–2 Oct), indicating this is meant to run unattended once configured.



2. Personas

Persona

Description

Campaign Experience

Eligible active user

Existing Capital Now app user in good standing (i.e., not Default or App Hold)

Sees full banner journey (1 → 2 → 3 → 4) and can submit a wish

Default / App Hold customer

User flagged Default or on App Hold per Capital Now's collections/risk status

Excluded entirely — does not see the campaign banner in any state, for the full campaign duration



3. Goals

Give eligible users a simple, low-friction way to submit one festive “wish” in-app.

Automatically transition the dashboard banner and its destination screen through four states, purely by date, with no manual ops trigger.

Reveal curated, pre-approved content on the Wall of Wishes — not real user submissions — to eliminate public user-generated-content risk.

Culminate the campaign with a highlights + winners reveal, recognising 5 users who will receive a gift (fulfilment owned by Marketing/Ops, outside this PRD's scope).













Layer 2 — Requirements & Execution

5. Functional Requirements

P0 — Must ship

Dashboard banner slot renders exactly one of four states, resolved by server date and user eligibility — nothing else competes for this slot during the campaign window.

Eligibility gate: Default and App Hold customers never see any campaign banner state, at any point in the campaign (14 Sept – 2 Oct).

Banner 1 (“Ganapati Bappa Morya!”, 14–25 Sept, not-yet-participated eligible users) → CTA “Write Your Wish” opens the Make a Wish screen.

Make a Wish screen: single free-text field, 120-character hard limit, optional “Your name” field, Submit CTA.

One wish submission per user for the entire campaign; resubmission is not allowed once a wish is sealed.

On submit → “Your Wish Is Sealed” confirmation screen with three actions: Back to Dashboard, Wall of Wishes, Share with Friends (quick-share bottom sheet), plus a top-left back control equivalent to Back to Dashboard.

After submission, the dashboard banner switches to Banner 2 (“Your wish is sealed”) for that user through 25 Sept; its CTA opens Wall of Wishes.

Wall of Wishes displays pre-seeded wishes supplied by the marketing/content team — never the viewing user's or any other user's actual submitted text — refreshed daily from 14–25 Sept.

From 26 Sept, Banner 1 and Banner 2 retire for every user (participant or not) and Banner 3 (“All wishes are in!”) takes over for all eligible users through 29 Sept, opening the Our Favourites screen (“The Highlights” + “A Few Favourites”, static highlight stats).

From 30 Sept–2 Oct, Banner 4 (“The Lucky wishes have been chosen”) opens the Winners screen — same static highlights, plus the winners/gift reveal for 5 users.

From 2 Oct onward, the campaign banner slot is fully retired for all users, with no fallback banner shown in its place.

Quick Share bottom sheet on the Wish Is Sealed screen (standard app-download link share, no custom tracking specified).

Scheduled daily re-shuffle of the Wall of Wishes entries, 14–25 Sept (content authored and supplied by Marketing).

6. Non-Functional Requirements

Submitted wish text and optional name are stored in admin panel but never surfaced in any public UI

Eligibility check (Default / App Hold flag) must be evaluated at banner render time and be consistent with the flag used elsewhere in the app.

7. Key Flows

Scenario 1 — user does not click Banner 1

Banner 1 remains on the dashboard, unchanged, from 14–25 September for any eligible user who never engages.

From 26 September, this user moves into the common post-25-September flow (Banner 3, then Banner 4) exactly like a user who did participate.

Scenario 2 — user clicks Banner 1

Banner 1 → Make a Wish → fill wish (≤120 characters) → Submit → Your Wish Is Sealed.

From Your Wish Is Sealed: Back to Dashboard or the back control → dashboard now shows Banner 2;Your wish is sealed page, back returns to dashboard on Banner 2; Share with Friends → quick-share bottom sheet.

Banner 2 remains through 25 September and reopens Your Wish Is Sealed / Wall of Wishes on tap.

Common flow from 26 September (all users, regardless of Scenario 1 or 2)

26–29 Sept: Banner 3 → Our Favourites screen (highlights + favourites).

30 Sept–2 Oct: Banner 4 → Winners screen (highlights + 5 winning wishes / gift reveal).

After 2 Oct: campaign banner slot is removed for all users.

8. Logic & Edge Cases

Default/App Hold status is evaluated at the time the banner would render; if a user is excluded, no campaign banner (in any state) appears for them for the full campaign duration.

Character counter and hard stop at 120 characters must be enforced client- and server-side on the Make a Wish field.

A user who already submitted a wish must never see Banner 1 or the Make a Wish screen again for the remainder of the campaign.

Wall of Wishes content is identical for all eligible users on a given day (it is not personalised or drawn from that user's own submission).

Banner state is purely a function of (a) today's date and (b) whether this user has submitted a wish — no other state should influence which banner shows.

13. Admin Panel — Wish Submissions Log (Master tab)

Purpose: Give Ops/Support an internal, searchable view of every wish submitted during the campaign, in the same list format already used for the AppHold/ticket table, so a wish can be looked up by CNID without touching the database.

Table structure

Wish Entered

Name Entered (optional)

Behaviour, matching the existing table:.

Sortable columns on CNID and Customer Name (sort arrows)

User Status pill styled the same way (e.g., "Eligible" / "App Hold" / "Default"), so this list visually matches other admin tables Ops already uses.

Search/filter by CNID and Customer Name, same as the existing ticket search, since that's the lookup key support agents will use.

Business Requirements Document (BRD)

AutomatiQA – AI-Powered Software Testing Platform

Project Name

AutomatiQA – AI-Powered Software Testing Platform

Business Objective

The objective of AutomatiQA is to simplify and automate software testing activities using artificial intelligence. The platform should help QA engineers, developers, and product teams reduce manual effort while improving test coverage and execution speed.

Business Requirements

Users must be able to create and manage testing projects within the platform. The system should allow users to upload requirement documents such as BRDs, user stories, and functional specifications.

AutomatiQA should analyze uploaded requirements and automatically generate relevant test scenarios and test cases using AI. Users should be able to review, edit, save, and execute generated test cases.

The platform should support multiple testing capabilities, including web UI testing, API testing, performance testing, and recorded browser workflows.

Users should also be able to select an AI provider and model, such as Gemini, OpenAI, or locally hosted Ollama models, based on available API credentials.

The system should provide dashboards displaying execution status, passed and failed tests, defects, and testing metrics.

Success Criteria

The solution should reduce manual test creation effort, improve requirement coverage, provide reusable test cases, and enable faster identification of application defects.
